primary.basis: Resolves to Mistral Large 3 (2512): 675B sparse MoE, 41B active, 256K ctx, text+image in (2.5B vision encoder). 14/16 ballots tagged Reasoning/IF/Math. Note: 1 source claimed text-only; 2 sources + vision-encoder spec say image input — majority wins.
Mistral Medium 3.5 (2604): 128B DENSE (no MoE), 256K ctx, text+image in, configurable reasoning, SWE-bench 77.6%. Skill's 'best-value' tier.
Mistral Small 4 (2603): dense, merges reasoning + vision + coding. ctx >=128K from family lineage (not independently verified). Function calling via API.
Mistral NeMo 12B (2407): dense, 128K ctx, text-only, Apache-2.0 2024-era workhorse.
Verified ALIAS of open-mistral-nemo-2407 — same model, same tags (not a separate tiny model).
Ministral 3 (3B dense, edge tier, Dec 2025 generation, Apache-2.0). 750 rpm budget router. 2 ballots tagged Coding — dropped as not a defining strength for a 3B edge model.
Ministral 3 (8B dense, edge tier); 8B line carries >=128K ctx (128K on 2410 predecessor; not independently re-verified).
Codestral (2508 snapshot): dedicated code model, FIM + function calling, 256K-class ctx.
Verified ALIAS: also resolves to codestral-2508 — identical tags to codestral-latest.
Magistral Medium (2509): Mistral's dedicated reasoning line (step-by-step thinking). 128K-class ctx (1.2). Base Medium 3 is multimodal but image input on Magistral not confirmed -> Vision withheld.
May 2026 flagship Flash: text/image/audio/video/PDF in, 1M ctx, 64K out, dynamic thinking; beats Gemini 3.1 Pro on agentic/coding benchmarks. Skill's scarcest tier (20 req/day).
Lite tier of 3.5: same multimodal stack + 1M ctx + thinking levels; coding/math deliberately weaker than Flash (withheld).
GA high-efficiency multimodal (text/image/video/audio/PDF), 1M ctx, thinking levels, OCR 90% (Roboflow). Answered 4/16 ballots in this very job — it's the router's fastest scarce route.
Gemini 3 Flash preview — foundation of the 3.5 Flash line: multimodal, 1M ctx, frontier agentic/coding/math at flash speed.
Ling 3.0 Flash: 124B MoE, 5.1B active, hybrid-linear attention (KDA+MLA), 262K ctx, thinking by default, agentic/SWE focus, TEXT-ONLY (2 ballots wrongly tagged Vision — web evidence overrides).
Nemotron 3 Super: 120B LatentMoE (Mamba-2 hybrid), 12B active, 1M ctx, reasoning on/off, built for agentic workflows/tool use/RAG; text-only.
Nemotron 3 Ultra: 550B LatentMoE, 55B active, 1M ctx, NVFP4, flagship — within ~8-10% of GPT-5.5 on HumanEval/LiveCodeBench; text-only. Skill tags it 'flagship,1M-ctx'.
Step 3.7 Flash: 198B sparse MoE VLM (196B LM + 1.8B perception encoder), ~11B active, 256K ctx, native image+VIDEO input, low/med/high reasoning, agentic search/planning, Apache-2.0.
META-ROUTE, not a model: Kilo's auto-selection shim that forwards to a backing model. Capability tags are undefined by design (they belong to whatever model it picks).
GPT-OSS-120B: 117B MoE, 5.1B active, 128K ctx, configurable reasoning (low/med/high), native tool use, text-only. 3/16 ballots here + skill's 'best-value,fast'.
Llama 3.3 70B: dense, 128K ctx, text-only, strong general assistant w/ function calling. Also the model that voted via HuggingFace in this job (Llama-3.1-8B variant).
Qwen3.6-27B: DENSE (not MoE), 27B, vision+text in, 262K native ctx (1M w/ YaRN), SWE-bench Verified 77.2% — beats the 397B MoE sibling on coding. Skill tags it 'code'.
Command A: 111B DENSE (A+ made the MoE switch later), 256K ctx, enterprise tool use / RAG / agents / multilingual; text-only. Skill tags 'best-value'.

ALIAS, not a fixed model: llm7.io's free-tier default backend (rotates). Tags undefined by design; 16/16-ish ballots still gave it general assistant tags (Reasoning/IF) since the backend is a capable chat model.
